sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña kārāpatanam uttamam agniṣṭomam avāpnoti munilokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Then, O knower of dharma, one should go to the most excellent Kārāpatana; there one attains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and proceeds to the world of sages.

sanskrit: saugandhikaṃ vanaṃ rājaṃs tato gaccheta mānavaḥ yatra brahmādayo devā ṛṣayaś ca tapodhanāḥ
english: Then, O king, a person should proceed to the Saugandhika forest, where Brahmā and the other gods dwell, and where the sages rich in austerities reside.

sanskrit: siddhacāraṇagandharvāḥ kiṃnarāḥ samahoragāḥ tad vanaṃ praviśann eva sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Siddhas, Cāraṇas, Gandharvas, Kiṃnaras, and great serpents inhabit that forest — merely by entering it one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: tato hi sā saricchreṣṭhā nadīnām uttamā nadī plakṣād devī srutā rājan mahāpuṇyā sarasvatī
english: For there flows that best of rivers, the supreme stream among all rivers — the goddess Sarasvatī, O king, issuing from the Plakṣa tree, supremely holy.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta valmīkān niḥsṛte jale arcayitvā pitṝn devān aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: There one should perform the ablution in the water that issues from the anthill; having honoured the ancestors and the gods, one obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: īśānādhyuṣitaṃ nāma tatra tīrthaṃ sudurlabham ṣaṭsu śamyānipāteṣu valmīkād iti niścayaḥ
english: That holy ford there, called Īśānādhyuṣita and exceedingly rare, lies within the distance of six throws of a śamyā stick from the anthill — this is certain.

sanskrit: kapilānāṃ sahasraṃ ca vājimedhaṃ ca vindati tatra snātvā naravyāghra dṛṣṭam etat purātane
english: By bathing there, O tiger among men, one obtains the merit of a thousand tawny cows and of the Vājimedhā rite — this has been seen in ancient tradition.

sanskrit: sugandhāṃ śatakumbhāṃ ca pañcayajñāṃ ca bhārata abhigamya naraśreṣṭha svargaloke mahīyate
english: Having visited Sugandhā, Śatakumbhā, and Pañcayajñā, O Bhārata, the best of men is honoured in the heavenly world.

sanskrit: triśūlakhātaṃ tatraiva tīrtham āsādya bhārata tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta pitṛdevārcane rataḥ gāṇapatyaṃ sa labhate dehaṃ tyaktvā na saṃśayaḥ
english: Having reached that same ford known as Triśūlakhāta, O Bhārata, one should perform the ablution there, devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods; upon leaving the body that person attains lordship among Gaṇas — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra devyāḥ sthānaṃ sudurlabham śākaṃbharīti vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
english: Then, O best of kings, one should go to the exceedingly rare abode of the goddess known as Śākaṃbarī, renowned throughout the three worlds.

sanskrit: divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ hi śākena kila suvrata āhāraṃ sā kṛtavatī māsi māsi narādhipa
english: For a divine thousand years, O faithful one, she maintained herself on vegetables alone, subsisting on them month by month, O lord of men.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo 'bhyāgatās tatra devyā bhaktyā tapodhanāḥ ātithyaṃ ca kṛtaṃ teṣāṃ śākena kila bhārata tataḥ śākambharīty eva nāma tasyāḥ pratiṣṭhitam
english: Sages rich in austerities came there out of devotion to the goddess, and she offered them hospitality with vegetables, O Bhārata; from that act her name Śākambharī became established.

sanskrit: śākaṃbharīṃ samāsādya brahmacārī samāhitaḥ trirātram uṣitaḥ śākaṃ bhakṣayen niyataḥ śuciḥ
english: Having reached Śākaṃbarī, a celibate student, composed and intent, should stay three nights, eating only vegetables with restraint and purity.

sanskrit: śākāhārasya yat samyag varṣair dvādaśabhiḥ phalam tat phalaṃ tasya bhavati devyāś chandena bhārata
english: Whatever merit accrues from properly subsisting on vegetables for twelve years — that very merit becomes his through the grace of the goddess, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato gacchet suvarṇākṣaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam yatra viṣṇuḥ prasādārthaṃ rudram ārādhayat purā
english: Then one should go to Suvarṇākṣa, renowned in all three worlds, where Viṣṇu formerly propitiated Rudra in order to win his favour.

sanskrit: varāṃś ca subahūṃl lebhe daivateṣu sudurlabhān uktaś ca tripuraghnena parituṣṭena bhārata
english: He obtained very many boons, exceedingly rare even among the gods; and the destroyer of Tripura, being fully pleased, spoke to him, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: api cāsmat priyataro loke kṛṣṇa bhaviṣyasi tvan mukhaṃ ca jagat kṛtsnaṃ bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Even more dear to us than ourselves shall you be in the world, O Kṛṣṇa, and the entire universe shall face toward you — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tatrābhigamya rājendra pūjayitvā vṛṣadhvajam aśvamedham avāpnoti gāṇapatyaṃ ca vindati
english: Having gone there and worshipped the bearer of the bull-banner, O best of kings, one obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha and also attains lordship among the Gaṇas.

sanskrit: dhūmāvatīṃ tato gacchet triratropoṣito naraḥ manasā prārthitān kāmāṃl labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Then a person who has fasted three nights should go to Dhūmāvatī; he obtains whatever desires he has sought in his mind — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: devyās tu dakṣiṇārdhena rathāvarto narādhipa tatrāroheta dharmajña śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ mahādevaprasādād dhi gaccheta paramāṃ gatim
english: By the southern side of the goddess is the holy ford Rathāvarta, O lord of men; one who is faithful and has his senses under control should ascend there, O knower of dharma; through the grace of Mahādeva he attains the supreme destination.

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya gaccheta bharatarṣabha dhārāṃ nāma mahāprājña sarvapāpapraṇāśinīm tatra snātvā naravyāghra na śocati narādhipa
english: After circumambulating it in the clockwise direction, one should go, O bull of the Bhāratas, O greatly wise one, to the ford called Dhārā, which destroys all sins; having bathed there, O tiger among men, the lord of men grieves no more.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña namaskṛtya mahāgirim svargadvāreṇa yat tulyaṃ gaṅgādvāraṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: Then, O knower of dharma, one should go, having paid homage to the great mountain, to Gaṅgādvāra, which is equal to the very gate of heaven — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta koṭitīrthe samāhitaḥ puṇḍarīkam avāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: One should perform ablution there at Koṭitīrtha with a concentrated mind; one attains the Puṇḍarīka sacrifice and also lifts up one's lineage.

sanskrit: saptagaṅge trigaṅge ca śakrāvarte ca tarpayan devān pitṝṃś ca vidhivat puṇyaloke mahīyate
english: By duly offering libations to gods and ancestors at Saptagaṅgā, Trigaṅgā, and Śakrāvarta, one is honoured in the worlds of the meritorious.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanakhale snātvā trirātropoṣito naraḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Then a person who has fasted three nights and bathed at Kanakhala obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha and proceeds to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: kapilāvaṭaṃ ca gaccheta tīrthasevī narādhipa uṣyaikāṃ rajanīṃ tatra gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: A pilgrim, O lord of men, should also go to Kapilāvaṭa; by spending a single night there, one obtains the merit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: nāgarājasya rājendra kapilasya mahātmanāḥ tīrthaṃ kuruvaraśreṣṭha sarvalokeṣu viśrutam
english: O best of kings, the ford of the great-souled serpent-king Kapila, O best among the Kurus, is renowned in all the worlds.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta nāgatīrthe narādhipa kapilānāṃ sahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: One should perform ablution at that Nāgatīrtha, O lord of men; a person thereby obtains the merit of a thousand tawny cows.

sanskrit: tato lalitikāṃ gacchec chaṃtanos tīrtham uttamam tatra snātvā naro rājan na durgatim avāpnuyāt
english: Then one should go to Lalitikā, the most excellent ford of Śaṃtanu; having bathed there, O king, a person does not reach an evil fate.

sanskrit: gaṅgāsaṃgamayoś caiva snāti yaḥ saṃgame naraḥ daśāśvamedhān āpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: A person who bathes at the confluence of the Gaṅgā — at those two meeting-points — obtains the merit of ten Aśvamedha sacrifices and also lifts up his lineage.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra sugandhāṃ lokaviśrutām sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā brahmaloke mahīyate
english: Then, O best of kings, one should go to Sugandhā, renowned throughout the worlds; with soul purified of all sins, one is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: rudrāvartaṃ tato gacchet tīrthasevī narādhipa tatra snātvā naro rājan svargaloke mahīyate
english: A pilgrim, O lord of men, should then go to Rudrāvarta; having bathed there, O king, a person is honoured in the heavenly world.

sanskrit: gaṅgāyāś ca naraśreṣṭha sarasvatyāś ca saṃgame snāto 'śvamedham āpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: One who bathes at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the Sarasvatī, O best of men, obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha and proceeds to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: bhadrakarṇeśvaraṃ gatvā devam arcya yathāvidhi na durgatim avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Having gone to Bhadrakarṇeśvara and worshipped the god according to proper rite, one does not reach an evil fate and proceeds to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: tataḥ kubjāmrakaṃ gacchet tīrthasevī yathākramam gosahasram avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: A pilgrim should then go to Kubjāmraka in due sequence; one obtains the merit of a thousand cows and proceeds to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: arundhatīvaṭaṃ gacchet tīrthasevī narādhipa sāmudrakam upaspṛśya trirātropoṣito naraḥ gosahasraphalaṃ vindet kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: A pilgrim, O lord of men, should go to Arundhatīvaṭa; by touching the ocean-ford after fasting three nights, a person obtains the merit of a thousand cows and also lifts up his lineage.

sanskrit: brahmāvartaṃ tato gacched brahmacārī samāhitaḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: A celibate student, composed in mind, should then go to Brahmāvarta; he obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha and proceeds to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: yamunāprabhavaṃ gatvā upaspṛśya ca yāmune aśvamedhaphalaṃ labdhvā svargaloke mahīyate
english: Having gone to the source of the Yamunā and touched its waters, one obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha and is honoured in the heavenly world.

sanskrit: darvīsaṃkramaṇaṃ prāpya tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam aśvamedham avāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Having reached the ford Darvīsaṃkramaṇa, renowned throughout the three worlds, one obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha and proceeds to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: sindhoś ca prabhavaṃ gatvā siddhagandharvasevitam tatroṣya rajanīḥ pañca vindyād bahu suvarṇakam
english: Having gone to the source of the Sindhu, frequented by Siddhas and Gandharvas, by staying there five nights one gains much gold.

sanskrit: atha vedīṃ samāsādya naraḥ paramadurgamām aśvamedham avāpnoti gacchec cauśanasīṃ gatim
english: Then, having reached the Vedī, which is most difficult of access, a person obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha and attains the destination taught by Uśanas.

sanskrit: ṛṣikulyāṃ samāsādya vāsiṣṭhaṃ caiva bhārata vāsiṣṭhaṃ samatikramya sarve varṇā dvijātayaḥ
english: Having reached the Ṛṣikulyā and also the Vāsiṣṭha ford, O Bhārata, by crossing beyond the Vāsiṣṭha, all the castes become twice-born.

sanskrit: ṛṣikulyāṃ naraḥ snātvā ṛṣilokaṃ prapadyate yadi tatra vasen māsaṃ śākāhāro narādhipa
english: A person who bathes in the Ṛṣikulyā attains the world of the sages; if he stays there a month subsisting on vegetables, O lord of men, he reaches the world of the sages.

sanskrit: bhṛgutuṅgaṃ samāsādya vājimedhaphalaṃ labhet gatvā vīrapramokṣaṃ ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Having reached Bhṛgutuṅga, one obtains the fruit of the Vājimedhā; and by going to Vīrapramokṣa, one is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: kṛttikāmaghayoś caiva tīrtham āsādya bhārata agniṣṭomātirātrābhyāṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti puṇyakṛt
english: Having reached the ford at the junction of Kṛttikā and Maghā, O Bhārata, a person of meritorious deeds obtains the combined fruit of the Agniṣṭoma and Atirātra sacrifices.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdhyāṃ samāsādya vidyātīrtham anuttamam upaspṛśya ca vidyānāṃ sarvāsāṃ pārago bhavet
english: Then, having reached Saṃdhyā and touched the incomparable ford of knowledge, Vidyātīrtha, one becomes accomplished in all branches of learning.

sanskrit: mahāśrame vased rātriṃ sarvapāpapramocane ekakālaṃ nirāhāro lokān āvasate śubhān
english: One who stays the night at Mahāśrama, which releases one from all sins, and eats but once a day or fasts completely, inhabits auspicious worlds.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭhakālopavāsena māsam uṣya mahālaye sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā vindyād bahu suvarṇakam
english: By fasting at the sixth part of the day and staying a month at Mahālaya, one whose soul is purified of all sins gains much gold.

sanskrit: atha vetasikāṃ gatvā pitāmahaniṣevitām aśvamedham avāpnoti gacchec cauśanasīṃ gatim
english: Then, having gone to Vetasikā, frequented by the Grandfather Brahmā himself, one obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha and attains the destination taught by Uśanas.

sanskrit: atha sundarikātīrthaṃ prāpya siddhaniṣevitam rūpasya bhāgī bhavati dṛṣṭam etat purātane
english: Then, having reached the ford of Sundarikā, frequented by Siddhas, one becomes endowed with beauty — this has been seen in ancient tradition.

sanskrit: tato vai brāhmaṇīṃ gatvā brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ padmavarṇena yānena brahmalokaṃ prapadyate
english: Then a celibate student with senses subdued, having gone to the Brāhmaṇī river, attains the world of Brahmā riding in a lotus-hued vehicle.

sanskrit: tataś ca naimiṣaṃ gacchet puṇyaṃ siddhaniṣevitam tatra nityaṃ nivasati brahmā devagaṇair vṛtaḥ
english: Then one should go to the holy Naimiṣa, frequented by Siddhas, where Brahmā eternally dwells, surrounded by hosts of gods.

sanskrit: naimiṣaṃ prārthayānasya pāpasyārdhaṃ praṇaśyati praviṣṭamātras tu naraḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: For one who merely longs for Naimiṣa, half his sin is destroyed; a person who has but entered it is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: tatra māsaṃ vased dhīro naimiṣe tīrthatatparaḥ pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni naimiṣe tāni bhārata
english: A wise person devoted to holy fords should stay a month at Naimiṣa; whatever holy fords exist on earth are all contained in Naimiṣa, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: abhiṣekakṛtas tatra niyato niyatāśanaḥ gavāmayasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti bhārata punāty āsaptamaṃ caiva kulaṃ bharatasattama
english: One who performs ablution there with self-control and regulated diet obtains the fruit of the Gavāmayana sacrifice, O Bhārata, and purifies his lineage even to the seventh generation, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yas tyajen naimiṣe prāṇān upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ sa modet svargalokastha evam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ nityaṃ puṇyaṃ ca medhyaṃ ca naimiṣaṃ nṛpasattama
english: One who abandons his life at Naimiṣa while fully devoted to fasting rejoices having attained the heavenly world — so say the wise ones; Naimiṣa is ever holy and pure, O best of kings.

sanskrit: gaṅgodbhedaṃ samāsādya trirātropoṣito naraḥ vājapeyam avāpnoti brahmabhūtaś ca jāyate
english: A person who has fasted three nights, having reached Gaṅgodbheda, obtains the merit of the Vājapeya sacrifice and is born merged with Brahmā.

sanskrit: sarasvatīṃ samāsādya tarpayet pitṛdevatāḥ sārasvateṣu lokeṣu modate nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Having reached the Sarasvatī and offered libations to ancestors and gods, one rejoices in the worlds of Sarasvatī — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tataś ca bāhudāṃ gacched brahmacārī samāhitaḥ devasatrasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: Then a celibate student, composed in mind, should go to the Bāhudā; a person thereby obtains the fruit of the Devasatra sacrifice.

sanskrit: tataś cīravatīṃ gacchet puṇyāṃ puṇyatamair vṛtām pitṛdevārcanarato vājapeyam avāpnuyāt
english: Then one should go to the holy Cīravatī, thronged with the most meritorious souls; devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods, one obtains the merit of the Vājapeya.

sanskrit: vimalāśokam āsādya virājati yathā śaśī tatroṣya rajanīm ekāṃ svargaloke mahīyate
english: Having reached Vimalāśoka, one shines like the moon; by staying there a single night one is honoured in the heavenly world.

sanskrit: gopratāraṃ tato gacchet sarayvās tīrtham uttamam yatra rāmo gataḥ svargaṃ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ
english: Then one should go to Gopratāra, the most excellent ford of the Sarayū, where Rāma ascended to heaven together with his servants, forces, and mounts.

sanskrit: dehaṃ tyaktvā divaṃ yātas tasya tīrthasya tejasā rāmasya ca prasādena vyavasāyāc ca bhārata
english: He departed to heaven having left his body, through the power of that ford and by the grace of Rāma and by his own determination, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tīrthe naraḥ snātvā gopratāre narādhipa sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā svargaloke mahīyate
english: A person who bathes at that ford, Gopratāra, O lord of men, with his soul purified of all sins, is honoured in the heavenly world.

sanskrit: rāmatīrthe naraḥ snātvā gomatyāṃ kurunandana aśvamedham avāpnoti punāti ca kulaṃ naraḥ
english: A person who bathes at the ford of Rāma on the Gomatī, O joy of the Kurus, obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha and purifies his lineage.

sanskrit: śatasāhasrikaṃ tatra tīrthaṃ bharatasattama tatropasparśanaṃ kṛtvā niyato niyatāśanaḥ gosahasraphalaṃ puṇyaṃ prāpnoti bharatarṣabha
english: There exists there a ford worth a hundred thousand, O best of the Bhāratas; by touching it with self-discipline and regulated diet, one obtains the holy merit of a thousand cows, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra bhartṛsthānam anuttamam koṭitīrthe naraḥ snātvā arcayitvā guhaṃ nṛpa gosahasraphalaṃ vindet tejasvī ca bhaven naraḥ
english: Then, O best of kings, one should go to the incomparable abode of the Lord; having bathed at Koṭitīrtha and worshipped Guha, O king, a person obtains the merit of a thousand cows and becomes radiant.

sanskrit: tato vārāṇasīṃ gatvā arcayitvā vṛṣadhvajam kapilāhrade naraḥ snātvā rājasūyaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then, having gone to Vārāṇasī and worshipped the bearer of the bull-banner, a person who bathes in the Kapilāhrada obtains the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeyasya rājendra tīrtham āsādya durlabham gomatīgaṅgayoś caiva saṃgame lokaviśrute agniṣṭomam avāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: Having reached the rare ford of Mārkaṇḍeya, O best of kings, at the world-renowned confluence of the Gomatī and the Gaṅgā, one obtains the merit of the Agniṣṭoma and also lifts up one's lineage.

sanskrit: tato gayāṃ samāsādya brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti gamanād eva bhārata
english: Then a celibate student with senses subdued, having reached Gayā, obtains the merit of the Aśvamedha by the very act of going there, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatrākṣayavaṭo nāma triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ pitṝṇāṃ tatra vai dattam akṣayaṃ bhavati prabho
english: There is the famous Akṣayavaṭa, renowned in all three worlds; whatever is offered there to the ancestors becomes imperishable, O lord.

sanskrit: mahānadyām upaspṛśya tarpayet pitṛdevatāḥ akṣayān prāpnuyāl lokān kulaṃ caiva samuddharet
english: Having touched the waters of the great river and offered libations to ancestors and gods, one attains imperishable worlds and also lifts up one's lineage.

sanskrit: tato brahmasaro gacched dharmāraṇyopaśobhitam pauṇḍarīkam avāpnoti prabhātām eva śarvarīm
english: Then one should go to Brahmasaras, beautified by the Dharmaraṇya forest; one obtains the Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice even by the dawn of the very same night.

sanskrit: tasmin sarasi rājendra brahmaṇo yūpa ucchritaḥ yūpaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā vājapeyaphalaṃ labhet
english: In that lake, O best of kings, stands the sacrificial post of Brahmā; by circumambulating that post clockwise, one obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra dhenukāṃ lokaviśrutām ekarātroṣito rājan prayacchet tiladhenukām sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā somalokaṃ vrajed dhruvam
english: Then, O best of kings, one should go to Dhenukā, renowned throughout the world; having stayed one night, O king, one should offer a cow of sesame — with soul purified of all sins one certainly reaches the world of Soma.

sanskrit: tatra cihnaṃ mahārāja adyāpi hi na saṃśayaḥ kapilā saha vatsena parvate vicaraty uta savatsāyāḥ padāni sma dṛśyante 'dyāpi bhārata
english: There is a sign there, O great king, and even today it is beyond doubt: a tawny cow roams the mountain with her calf, and the footprints of that cow with calf are visible even today, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: teṣūpaspṛśya rājendra padeṣu nṛpasattama yat kiṃ cid aśubhaṃ karma tat praṇaśyati bhārata
english: By touching those footprints, O best of kings, O best of lords, whatever inauspicious deeds one may have done are destroyed, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato gṛdhravaṭaṃ gacchet sthānaṃ devasya dhīmataḥ snāyīta bhasmanā tatra abhigamya vṛṣadhvajam
english: Then one should go to Gṛdhravaṭa, the abode of the wise God; having approached the bearer of the bull-banner there, one should bathe with ashes.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇena bhavec cīrṇaṃ vrataṃ dvādaśavārṣikam itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ sarvapāpaṃ praṇaśyati
english: For a brahmin this equals the observance of a twelve-year vow; for persons of the other castes all sins are destroyed.

sanskrit: gaccheta tata udyantaṃ parvataṃ gītanāditam sāvitraṃ tu padaṃ tatra dṛśyate bharatarṣabha
english: Then one should go to the Udyanta mountain, resounding with songs; there the foot-print of the Sāvitrī is seen, O bull of the Bhāratas.
